editorial:
Imagine walking into a job where you think you have found a best friend, but that person is actually tracking your every move. You get to see this play out between a lonely, older teacher and a bubbly new art teacher who makes a huge mistake by dating a student. The vibe is super tense and uncomfortable because you can tell something bad is about to happen. It feels like a game of cat and mouse where the stakes are your entire career and reputation. You will find yourself rooting for the young teacher while also feeling scared for her.

What really makes this work is the acting. Judi Dench is scary as the controlling friend, and Cate Blanchett is great as the panicked teacher. The story moves quickly and keeps you guessing about who is actually the villain here. If you enjoy dramas with lots of secrets and power trips, you will love this.
endingExplained: Everything falls apart when the older teacher, Sheba, reveals she has been keeping a diary of all her friend's secrets. She uses this to blackmail the art teacher. By the end, the young teacher loses her job and her marriage. The older teacher wins the power struggle, but she ends up more alone than ever. She stays at the school, but everyone knows she is cold and calculating, leaving her isolated in her victory.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological thrillers and great acting.
